classification.difficultyReason: Choose useful coordinates to test each rule and match the resulting points to the supplied graphs, distinguishing lines with the same direction through their positions.

inlines.text: Match the rules A–D with the graphs a–d.

spec.description: Unit Cartesian grid, sparse labelled ticks, marked intercepts and a descending line. The origin O is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: x range -2 to 3; y range -2 to 4; grid step 1; y=-x+2; marked points (0,2) and (2,0).
spec.answerVisibility: All graph givens remain visible; no rule match is printed.

spec.answerVisibility: All graph givens remain visible; no rule match is printed.

spec.description: Unit Cartesian grid, ascending line and two marked points, with the negative coordinate annotation left of its point. The x=-1 tick label is above its tick to separate negative labels near the origin; O is omitted.
spec.mathematics: x range -3 to 3; y range -2 to 4; grid step 1; y=2x+1; marked points (0,1) and (-1,-1); bounded line from (-1.5,-2) to (1.5,4).
spec.answerVisibility: All graph givens remain visible; no rule match is printed.

spec.description: Unit Cartesian grid and descending line through marked negative intercepts. The x=-1 tick label is above its tick to separate negative labels near the origin; O is omitted.
spec.mathematics: x range -3 to 2; y range -3 to 3; grid step 1; y=-x-1; marked points (-1,0) and (0,-1); bounded line from (-3,2) to (2,-3).
spec.answerVisibility: All graph givens remain visible; no rule match is printed.

answer.short: A – c, B – d, C – b, D – a.
answer.worked:
Substitute two $x$ values into each rule and match the resulting points to a graph.

A: $x=-1,0$ gives $y=-1,1$, so the points are $(-1,-1)$ and $(0,1)$: graph c.

B: $x=-1,0$ gives $y=0,-1$, so the points are $(-1,0)$ and $(0,-1)$: graph d.

C: $x=1,2$ gives $y=1,-1$, so the points are $(1,1)$ and $(2,-1)$: graph b.

D: $x=0,2$ gives $y=2,0$, so the points are $(0,2)$ and $(2,0)$: graph a.
